verses.greek: Τότε οὖν ἔλαβεν ὁ Πιλᾶτος τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἐμαστίγωσεν.
verses.literal: At that time therefore took the Pilate the Jesus and flogged Him.
verses.dgt: Then Pilate took Jesus and had him scourged.

verses.greek: καὶ οἱ στρατιῶται πλέξαντες στέφανον ἐξ ἀκανθῶν ἐπέθηκαν αὐτοῦ τῇ κεφαλῇ, καὶ ἱμάτιον πορφυροῦν περιέβαλον αὐτόν,
verses.literal: And the soldiers having twisted together a crown of thorns put it of Him on the head and a robe purple cast around Him
verses.dgt: And the soldiers, having woven a crown from thorns, put it on his head and wrapped him in a purple garment.

verses.greek: καὶ ἤρχοντο πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ ἔλεγον· Χαῖρε, ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων· καὶ ἐδίδοσαν αὐτῷ ῥαπίσματα.
verses.literal: and they were coming up to Him and were saying Hail! O King of the Jews! And they were giving to Him blows with the palm.
verses.dgt: They were coming to him and saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!” and they were giving him slaps.

verses.greek: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν πάλιν ἔξω ὁ Πιλᾶτος καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἴδε ἄγω ὑμῖν αὐτὸν ἔξω, ἵνα γνῶτε ὅτι οὐδεμίαν αἰτίαν εὑρίσκω ἐν αὐτῷ.
verses.literal: And went forth again outside the Pilate and he says to them Behold I bring to you Him out so that you may know that no thing guilt I find in Him.
verses.dgt: And Pilate went outside again and says to them, “Look, I am bringing him out to you so that you may know that I find no charge in him.”

verses.greek: ἐξῆλθεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἔξω, φορῶν τὸν ἀκάνθινον στέφανον καὶ τὸ πορφυροῦν ἱμάτιον. καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἰδοὺ ὁ ἄνθρωπος.
verses.literal: Went forth therefore the Jesus outside wearing the thorny crown and the purple robe. And he says to them behold the man!
verses.dgt: So Jesus came outside, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple garment. And Pilate says to them, “Look—the man!”

verses.greek: ὅτε οὖν εἶδον αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ ὑπηρέται ἐκραύγασαν λέγοντες· Σταύρωσον σταύρωσον. λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Λάβετε αὐτὸν ὑμεῖς καὶ σταυρώσατε, ἐγὼ γὰρ οὐχ εὑρίσκω ἐν αὐτῷ αἰτίαν.
verses.literal: When therefore saw Him the chief priests and the officers they cried out saying do crucify do crucify Says to them the Pilate do take Him yourselves and do crucify him I myself for no find in Him guilt.
verses.dgt: So when the chief priests and the officers saw him, they cried out, saying, “Crucify! Crucify!” Pilate says to them, “Take him yourselves and crucify him, for I find no charge in him.”

verses.greek: ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι· Ἡμεῖς νόμον ἔχομεν, καὶ κατὰ τὸν νόμον ὀφείλει ἀποθανεῖν, ὅτι υἱὸν θεοῦ ἑαυτὸν ἐποίησεν.
verses.literal: Answered to him the Jews We ourselves a law have and according to the law He ought to die because the Son of God Himself He made.
verses.dgt: The Jews answered him, “We have a law, and according to the law he ought to die, because he made himself Son of God.”

verses.greek: Ὅτε οὖν ἤκουσεν ὁ Πιλᾶτος τοῦτον τὸν λόγον, μᾶλλον ἐφοβήθη,
verses.literal: When therefore heard the Pilate this the word the more he was afraid
verses.dgt: So when Pilate heard this statement, he became even more afraid,

verses.greek: καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸ πραιτώριον πάλιν καὶ λέγει τῷ Ἰησοῦ· Πόθεν εἶ σύ; ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἀπόκρισιν οὐκ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ.
verses.literal: And he went into the Praetorium again and he says the to Jesus From where are You yourself? the But Jesus an answer not did give to him.
verses.dgt: and he entered the governor’s headquarters again and says to Jesus, “Where are you from?” But Jesus gave him no answer.

verses.greek: λέγει οὖν αὐτῷ ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Ἐμοὶ οὐ λαλεῖς; οὐκ οἶδας ὅτι ἐξουσίαν ἔχω ἀπολῦσαί σε καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἔχω σταυρῶσαί σε;
verses.literal: Says therefore to Him the Pilate To me myself not speak You? Surely You know that authority I have to release You and authority I have to crucify You?
verses.dgt: So Pilate says to him, “You do not speak to me? Do you not know that I have authority to release you and authority to crucify you?”

verses.greek: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐκ εἶχες ἐξουσίαν κατʼ ἐμοῦ οὐδεμίαν εἰ μὴ ἦν δεδομένον σοι ἄνωθεν· διὰ τοῦτο ὁ παραδούς μέ σοι μείζονα ἁμαρτίαν ἔχει.
verses.literal: Answered to him Jesus Not you were having authority against Me none only unless it were given to you from above Because of this the one having betrayed Me to you greater sin has.
verses.dgt: Jesus answered him, “You would have no authority against me at all unless it had been given to you from above. For this reason the one who handed me over to you has greater sin.”

verses.greek: ἐκ τούτου ὁ Πιλᾶτος ἐζήτει ἀπολῦσαι αὐτόν· οἱ δὲ Ἰουδαῖοι ἐκραύγασαν λέγοντες· Ἐὰν τοῦτον ἀπολύσῃς, οὐκ εἶ φίλος τοῦ Καίσαρος· πᾶς ὁ βασιλέα ἑαυτὸν ποιῶν ἀντιλέγει τῷ Καίσαρι.
verses.literal: Out of this the Pilate was seeking to release Him. the but the Jews cried out saying If this man you shall release not you are a friend the of Caesar. Everyone the a king himself making speaks against the Caesar.
verses.dgt: From this point Pilate was seeking to release him, but the Jews cried out, saying, “If you release this man, you are not Caesar’s friend. Everyone who makes himself a king speaks against Caesar.”

verses.greek: Ὁ οὖν Πιλᾶτος ἀκούσας τῶν λόγων τούτων ἤγαγεν ἔξω τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἐπὶ βήματος εἰς τόπον λεγόμενον Λιθόστρωτον, Ἑβραϊστὶ δὲ Γαββαθα.
verses.literal: the Therefore Pilate having heard the words these brought out the Jesus and sat down upon judgment seat at a place being named the Stone Pavement in Hebrew now Gabbatha.
verses.dgt: So Pilate, having heard these words, brought Jesus outside and sat down on the judgment seat at a place called the Stone Pavement, but in Hebrew Gabbatha.

verses.greek: ἦν δὲ παρασκευὴ τοῦ πάσχα, ὥρα ἦν ὡς ἕκτη. καὶ λέγει τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις· Ἴδε ὁ βασιλεὺς ὑμῶν.
verses.literal: It was now the Day of Preparation of the Passover the hour was about the sixth. And he says to the Jews Behold the king of you!
verses.dgt: Now it was the day of preparation for the Passover; it was about the sixth hour. And he says to the Jews, “Look, your King!”

verses.greek: ἐκραύγασαν οὖν ἐκεῖνοι· Ἆρον ἆρον, σταύρωσον αὐτόν. λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Τὸν βασιλέα ὑμῶν σταυρώσω; ἀπεκρίθησαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς· Οὐκ ἔχομεν βασιλέα εἰ μὴ Καίσαρα.
verses.literal: They cried out therefore concerning Him: away away! do crucify Him! Says to them the Pilate The King of you shall I crucify? Answered the chief priests Not we have a king only except Caesar.
verses.dgt: So they cried out, “Away with him! Away with him! Crucify him!” Pilate says to them, “Shall I crucify your King?” The chief priests answered, “We have no king except Caesar.”

verses.greek: τότε οὖν παρέδωκεν αὐτὸν αὐτοῖς ἵνα σταυρωθῇ. Παρέλαβον οὖν τὸν Ἰησοῦν·
verses.literal: Then therefore he delivered Him to them that He may be crucified. They took therefore the Jesus
verses.dgt: Then he handed him over to them so that he might be crucified. So they took Jesus,

verses.greek: καὶ βαστάζων αὑτῷ τὸν σταυρὸν ἐξῆλθεν εἰς τὸν λεγόμενον Κρανίου Τόπον, ὃ λέγεται Ἑβραϊστὶ Γολγοθα,
verses.literal: And bearing His own the cross He went out to the place being named of the Skull Place which is named in Hebrew Golgotha
verses.dgt: and carrying the cross for himself, he went out to the place called Place of a Skull, which is called Golgotha in Hebrew,

verses.greek: ὅπου αὐτὸν ἐσταύρωσαν, καὶ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ἄλλους δύο ἐντεῦθεν καὶ ἐντεῦθεν, μέσον δὲ τὸν Ἰησοῦν.
verses.literal: where Him they crucified and with Him others two on this side and on that side in between now the Jesus.
verses.dgt: where they crucified him, and with him two others, one on each side, and Jesus in the middle.

verses.greek: ἔγραψεν δὲ καὶ τίτλον ὁ Πιλᾶτος καὶ ἔθηκεν ἐπὶ τοῦ σταυροῦ· ἦν δὲ γεγραμμένον· Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων.
verses.literal: Wrote then also a title the Pilate and put it on the cross. It was now written: Jesus the of Nazareth the King of the Jews.
verses.dgt: Pilate also wrote a title and put it on the cross. It was written: “Jesus the Nazarene, the King of the Jews.”

verses.greek: τοῦτον οὖν τὸν τίτλον πολλοὶ ἀνέγνωσαν τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ὅτι ἐγγὺς ἦν ὁ τόπος τῆς πόλεως ὅπου ἐσταυρώθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς· καὶ ἦν γεγραμμένον Ἑβραϊστί, Ῥωμαϊστί, Ἑλληνιστί.
verses.literal: This therefore the title many read of the Jews for near was the place of the city where was crucified the Jesus and it was written in Hebrew in Latin in Greek.
verses.dgt: So many of the Jews read this title, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city, and it was written in Hebrew, Latin, and Greek.

verses.greek: ἔλεγον οὖν τῷ Πιλάτῳ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς τῶν Ἰουδαίων· Μὴ γράφε· Ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἀλλʼ ὅτι ἐκεῖνος εἶπεν Βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων εἰμί.
verses.literal: Were saying therefore the to Pilate the chief priests of the Jews Not do write The King of the Jews but for He said King of the Jews. I am
verses.dgt: So the chief priests of the Jews were saying to Pilate, “Do not write, ‘The King of the Jews,’ but that he said, ‘I am King of the Jews.’”

verses.greek: ἀπεκρίθη ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Ὃ γέγραφα γέγραφα.
verses.literal: Answered the Pilate What I have written I have written.
verses.dgt: Pilate answered, “What I have written, I have written.”

verses.greek: οἱ οὖν στρατιῶται ὅτε ἐσταύρωσαν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἔλαβον τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐποίησαν τέσσαρα μέρη, ἑκάστῳ στρατιώτῃ μέρος, καὶ τὸν χιτῶνα. ἦν δὲ ὁ χιτὼν ἄραφος, ἐκ τῶν ἄνωθεν ὑφαντὸς διʼ ὅλου·
verses.literal: The then soldiers when they crucified the Jesus took the garments of Him and made four parts to each soldier a part and also the tunic. Was now the tunic seamless from the top woven throughout all.
verses.dgt: So when the soldiers crucified Jesus, they took his garments and made four parts, a part for each soldier, and also the tunic. Now the tunic was seamless, woven from the top throughout.

verses.greek: εἶπαν οὖν πρὸς ἀλλήλους· Μὴ σχίσωμεν αὐτόν, ἀλλὰ λάχωμεν περὶ αὐτοῦ τίνος ἔσται· ἵνα ἡ γραφὴ πληρωθῇ ἡ λέγουσα· Διεμερίσαντο τὰ ἱμάτιά μου ἑαυτοῖς καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν ἱματισμόν μου ἔβαλον κλῆρον. Οἱ μὲν οὖν στρατιῶται ταῦτα ἐποίησαν.
verses.literal: They said therefore to one another Not let us tear up it but let us cast lots for it whose it will be that the Scripture may be fulfilled what is being spoken: They divided the garments of Mine among themselves and for the clothing of Mine they cast a lot. The indeed therefore soldiers these things did
verses.dgt: So they said to one another, “Let us not tear it, but let us cast lots for it, to see whose it will be,” so that the Scripture might be fulfilled which says, “They divided my garments among themselves, and for my clothing they cast a lot.” So the soldiers did these things.

verses.greek: Εἱστήκεισαν δὲ παρὰ τῷ σταυρῷ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἡ ἀδελφὴ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ, Μαρία ἡ τοῦ Κλωπᾶ καὶ Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνή.
verses.literal: Had been standing however by the cross the of Jesus the mother of Him and the sister of the mother of Him Mary the wife the of Clopas and Mary the Magdalene.
verses.dgt: Now standing beside the cross of Jesus were his mother, his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.

verses.greek: Ἰησοῦς οὖν ἰδὼν τὴν μητέρα καὶ τὸν μαθητὴν παρεστῶτα ὃν ἠγάπα λέγει τῇ μητρί· Γύναι, ἴδε ὁ υἱός σου·
verses.literal: Jesus therefore having seen the His mother and the disciple already standing by whom He was loving says to the mother Woman behold the son of you.
verses.dgt: So Jesus, seeing his mother and the disciple whom he loved standing nearby, says to his mother, “Woman, look—your son.”

verses.greek: εἶτα λέγει τῷ μαθητῇ· Ἴδε ἡ μήτηρ σου. καὶ ἀπʼ ἐκείνης τῆς ὥρας ἔλαβεν ὁ μαθητὴς αὐτὴν εἰς τὰ ἴδια.
verses.literal: Then He says to the disciple behold the mother of you. And from that very the hour took the disciple her to the his own.
verses.dgt: Then he says to the disciple, “Look—your mother.” And from that hour the disciple took her into his own home.

verses.greek: Μετὰ τοῦτο εἰδὼς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἤδη πάντα τετέλεσται ἵνα τελειωθῇ ἡ γραφὴ λέγει· Διψῶ.
verses.literal: After this knowing the Jesus that now all things has been accomplished so that may be fulfilled the Scripture He says I thirst.
verses.dgt: After this, Jesus, knowing that by now all things had been completed, so that the Scripture might be completed, says, “I am thirsty.”

verses.greek: σκεῦος ἔκειτο ὄξους μεστόν· σπόγγον οὖν μεστὸν τοῦ ὄξους ὑσσώπῳ περιθέντες προσήνεγκαν αὐτοῦ τῷ στόματι.
verses.literal: A vessel was set there of sour wine full. a sponge therefore full of the sour wine on a hyssop stalk having put they brought it to the mouth.
verses.dgt: A vessel full of sour wine was standing there. So they put a sponge full of the sour wine on hyssop and brought it to his mouth.

verses.greek: ὅτε οὖν ἔλαβεν τὸ ὄξος ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Τετέλεσται, καὶ κλίνας τὴν κεφαλὴν παρέδωκεν τὸ πνεῦμα.
verses.literal: When then took the sour wine the Jesus He said It has been finished. And having bowed the head He yielded up the spirit.
verses.dgt: So when Jesus received the sour wine, he said, “It is completed,” and bowing his head, he gave up the spirit.

verses.greek: Οἱ οὖν Ἰουδαῖοι, ἐπεὶ παρασκευὴ ἦν, ἵνα μὴ μείνῃ ἐπὶ τοῦ σταυροῦ τὰ σώματα ἐν τῷ σαββάτῳ, ἦν γὰρ μεγάλη ἡ ἡμέρα ἐκείνου τοῦ σαββάτου, ἠρώτησαν τὸν Πιλᾶτον ἵνα κατεαγῶσιν αὐτῶν τὰ σκέλη καὶ ἀρθῶσιν.
verses.literal: the Therefore the Jews since the Preparation was so that not may remain on the cross the bodies on the Sabbath — was for a high the day of that the Sabbath — asked the Pilate that may be broken their the legs and they may be taken away.
verses.dgt: Then the Jews, since it was the day of preparation, so that the bodies would not remain on the cross on the Sabbath—for that Sabbath day was a great one—asked Pilate that their legs might be broken and they might be taken away.

verses.greek: ἦλθον οὖν οἱ στρατιῶται, καὶ τοῦ μὲν πρώτου κατέαξαν τὰ σκέλη καὶ τοῦ ἄλλου τοῦ συσταυρωθέντος αὐτῷ·
verses.literal: Came therefore the soldiers and of the indeed first broke the legs and of the other which having been crucified with Him.
verses.dgt: So the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first man and of the other one who had been crucified with him.

verses.greek: ἐπὶ δὲ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐλθόντες, ὡς εἶδον ἤδη αὐτὸν τεθνηκότα, οὐ κατέαξαν αὐτοῦ τὰ σκέλη,
verses.literal: to however the Jesus having come when they saw already Him having been dead not they did break His the legs
verses.dgt: But when they came to Jesus, seeing that he was already dead, they did not break his legs.

verses.greek: ἀλλʼ εἷς τῶν στρατιωτῶν λόγχῃ αὐτοῦ τὴν πλευρὰν ἔνυξεν, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν εὐθὺς αἷμα καὶ ὕδωρ.
verses.literal: But one of the soldiers with a spear of His the side pierced and came out immediately blood and water.
verses.dgt: Instead, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.

verses.greek: καὶ ὁ ἑωρακὼς μεμαρτύρηκεν, καὶ ἀληθινὴ αὐτοῦ ἐστιν ἡ μαρτυρία, καὶ ἐκεῖνος οἶδεν ὅτι ἀληθῆ λέγει, ἵνα καὶ ὑμεῖς πιστεύητε.
verses.literal: And the one having seen has borne witness and true of him is the testimony And He knows that truth he is speaking that also you yourselves may believe.
verses.dgt: And the one who has seen has testified, and his testimony is true, and he knows that he is telling the truth, so that you also may believe.

verses.greek: ἐγένετο γὰρ ταῦτα ἵνα ἡ γραφὴ πληρωθῇ· Ὀστοῦν οὐ συντριβήσεται αὐτοῦ.
verses.literal: Took place for these things so that the Scripture may be fulfilled: Bone not one will be broken of Him.
verses.dgt: For these things happened so that the Scripture might be fulfilled: “Not a bone of him will be broken.”

verses.greek: καὶ πάλιν ἑτέρα γραφὴ λέγει· Ὄψονται εἰς ὃν ἐξεκέντησαν.
verses.literal: And again another Scripture says: They will behold on the One they have pierced.
verses.dgt: And again another Scripture says, “They will look on the one whom they pierced.”

verses.greek: Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα ἠρώτησεν τὸν Πιλᾶτον Ἰωσὴφ ἀπὸ Ἁριμαθαίας, ὢν μαθητὴς τοῦ Ἰησοῦ κεκρυμμένος δὲ διὰ τὸν φόβον τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἵνα ἄρῃ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ· καὶ ἐπέτρεψεν ὁ Πιλᾶτος. ἦλθεν οὖν καὶ ἦρεν τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ.
verses.literal: After then these things asked the Pilate Joseph from Arimathea being a disciple the of Jesus — concealed however through the fear of the Jews — that he may take away the body the of Jesus. and gave permission the Pilate. He came therefore and he took away the body of Him.
verses.dgt: After these things Joseph from Arimathea, who was a disciple of Jesus but secretly because of fear of the Jews, asked Pilate that he might take away Jesus’ body. Pilate permitted it. So he came and took away his body.

verses.greek: ἦλθεν δὲ καὶ Νικόδημος, ὁ ἐλθὼν πρὸς αὐτὸν νυκτὸς τὸ πρῶτον, φέρων μίγμα σμύρνης καὶ ἀλόης ὡς λίτρας ἑκατόν.
verses.literal: Came now also Nicodemus the one having come to Him by night at the first bearing a mixture of myrrh and aloes about litras a hundred.
verses.dgt: Nicodemus also came—the one who had first come to him at night—bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about one hundred pounds.

verses.greek: ἔλαβον οὖν τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ ἔδησαν αὐτὸ ὀθονίοις μετὰ τῶν ἀρωμάτων, καθὼς ἔθος ἐστὶν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ἐνταφιάζειν.
verses.literal: They took therefore the body the of Jesus and bound it in linen cloths with the spices even as the custom is among the Jews to prepare for burial.
verses.dgt: So they took Jesus’ body and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, just as is the burial custom of the Jews.

verses.greek: ἦν δὲ ἐν τῷ τόπῳ ὅπου ἐσταυρώθη κῆπος, καὶ ἐν τῷ κήπῳ μνημεῖον καινόν, ἐν ᾧ οὐδέπω οὐδεὶς ἦν τεθειμένος·
verses.literal: There was now in the place where He was crucified a garden and in the garden a tomb new in which not yet no one was already laid.
verses.dgt: Now in the place where he was crucified there was a garden, and in the garden a new tomb in which no one had yet been laid.

verses.greek: ἐκεῖ οὖν διὰ τὴν παρασκευὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ὅτι ἐγγὺς ἦν τὸ μνημεῖον, ἔθηκαν τὸν Ἰησοῦν.
verses.literal: There therefore on account of the Preparation of the Jews because near was the tomb they laid the Jesus.
verses.dgt: So because of the Jewish day of preparation, since the tomb was nearby, they laid Jesus there.
